selectionReason: RC71 left a detector-level proxy failure whose practical meaning could be tested without opening artificial stars or Cepheid outcomes. The same experiment also exposes a general transport problem—support before loss—and a post-selection problem—how to adapt after a failed gate without optimizing on the failure.
newVerifiedFacts: The purity-oriented catalogue rule yields 260 six-pixel-isolated candidates in NRCB1 and 91 in NRCB2, with at least 21 and 14 respectively in every 2x2 cell.
At the physically motivated 10.2-pixel non-overlap distance, NRCB1 has only 49 candidates and its sparsest cell has four; NRCB2 has zero in all four cells.
The EE80-INDEPENDENT route therefore stops on support and computes no large-aperture residual.
The coordinate hash selected exactly eight core candidates per cell and detector, excluding every listed DOLPHOT PSF-training coordinate.
All sixteen original CAL files match the RC69 MAST manifest hashes before aperture integration.
The first core divergence is the NRCB1 control: p90 absolute residual is 0.302521 mag in F090W and 0.210339 mag in F150W, exceeding 0.03 mag.
NRCB1 retains cell-median ranges of 0.186440 and 0.204194 mag after one per-filter offset, so a global core fraction is not spatially stable at the required level.
NRCB2 detector medians are +0.302432 mag in F090W and +0.165408 mag in F150W, but they are not interpretable as detector effects because the control failed first.
NRCB2 also misses the valid-star minimum in one F090W cell, while the other candidate residual, tail, and spatial gates fail diagnostically.
Node independently reconstructs the control-only offsets, all valid measurement residuals, star medians, filter summaries, and gates from the Python output rows.
The original NRCB2 100-star PSF failure and the NRCB3-4, artificial-star, distance, and H0 closures are unchanged.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: A conventional non-overlapping EE80 aperture holdout has enough spatial support to adjudicate both detectors.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: Every 2x2 cell in NRCB1 and NRCB2 contains at least eight purity-selected stars separated by 10.2 pixels.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Rejected at support: NRCB1 minimum cell is four and NRCB2 has zero in every cell.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: A single per-filter core-aperture offset learned on NRCB1 leaves a sufficiently small control tail.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: NRCB1 p90 absolute residual is at most 0.03 mag in F090W and F150W.
hypothesisAdjudication.decision: Retire the exact core holdout before interpreting NRCB2.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: If the core adjudicator were qualified, its unchanged NRCB1 offset would transport to NRCB2 within 0.01 mag.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: Both detector medians and every cell median stay within 0.01 mag, p90 stays within 0.03 mag, and cell range stays within 0.02 mag.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Not adjudicable as a detector hypothesis because H72-B failed first; diagnostic NRCB2 values exceed all effect gates.
hypothesisAdjudication.decision: Do not estimate a detector correction from the failed diagnostic.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: A support-first adaptation DAG can preserve a failed proxy while testing a separate rescue without post-outcome threshold repair.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: The large-aperture branch stops on support, the core branch stops at the control, and neither path changes RC71 or opens downstream outcomes.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Supported for this execution and independently reproduced.
hypothesisAdjudication.decision: Retain the state-machine pattern for future measurement-operator rescues.

survivingHypotheses: NRCB2 may still have adequate PSF photometry; RC72 rejected adjudicators, not the underlying photometry.
A physics-based PSF or neighbor-aware scene model may separate aperture fraction, subpixel phase, and crowding better than a global small-core offset.
A disjoint tile or external calibration field may provide the isolated support missing from the current NRCB2 tile.
failedOrRejectedAttempts: The original 100-star gate remains failed; its threshold was not reduced to 91.
The EE80 large-aperture route was stopped before residuals because target support was zero.
The small-core route was retired at the NRCB1 control tail rather than recalibrated by cell or detector.

An initial Python execution stopped before producing an output because unsigned DQ data cannot be memory mapped under Astropy; rerunning with in-memory DQ loading changed no scientific rule and is recorded as an implementation failure.
NRCB2 diagnostic residuals were not promoted to a correction or a distance-ladder effect after the control failure.
minimumMeaningfulAdvance: A public isolated-star calibration field must first qualify WCS centering, subpixel integration, and a physics-based PSF or scene-model residual to the frozen tail bound; only then may a fresh, disjoint NGC 3447 holdout test detector transport.

newApproach.name: External integrator qualification followed by disjoint physics-PSF transport
newApproach.hypothesis: The large RC72 control tail is dominated by an unmodeled measurement operator—subpixel centering, spatial PSF fraction, neighbor wings, or local background—rather than irreducible source noise.
newApproach.difference: Instead of tuning aperture radii on NGC 3447, qualify the entire pixel-to-flux operator on isolated calibration stars with known spatial and subpixel coverage, freeze its nuisance model, then test it once on a disjoint target tile.
newApproach.bottleneck: The current adjudicator cannot tell detector error from its own spatially varying aperture fraction.
requirements: STPSF or an independently validated scene model
newApproach.firstTest: Select at least eight isolated calibration stars in each detector-position/subpixel stratum using WCS and catalogue metrics only. Before fitting target data, require the model to keep p90 absolute residual within 0.03 mag and cell-median range within 0.02 mag under leave-one-exposure-out validation.
newApproach.success: The external control passes every frozen support, tail, and spatial gate, and the unchanged model produces an interpretable fresh-tile NRCB1/NRCB2 contrast.
newApproach.reject: The external control repeats a tail above 0.03 mag or requires target-specific spatial offsets.
newApproach.stop: Stop on inadequate stratum support, a failed external control, leakage from the target tile, or disagreement between independent implementations.
newApproach.failureValue: Failure identifies whether centering, PSF physics, background, or crowding must be modeled before another detector claim is attempted.

workPackages.purpose: Qualify the adjudicator away from NGC 3447.
workPackages.method: Freeze an isolated-star calibration dataset and stratify by detector position, filter, and subpixel phase.
workPackages.input: Official CAL products, WCS and CRDS receipts, and a source list not derived from NGC 3447 residuals.
workPackages.output: External support manifest and leave-one-exposure-out residual ledger.
workPackages.pass: Every stratum has adequate support; p90 <=0.03 mag and spatial range <=0.02 mag.
workPackages.next: Localize the first nuisance term; do not open a target tile.

workPackages.purpose: Separate centering, PSF, neighbor, and background contributions.
workPackages.method: Compare fixed aperture, STPSF forward model, and neighbor-aware scene model under the same external stars and residual definition.
workPackages.input: External ledger from W72-1 and frozen model families.
workPackages.pass: One model passes without target-specific offsets and two implementations agree.
workPackages.fail: No model passes or selection changes after outcomes.
workPackages.next: Acquire additional calibration support or stop the rescue program.

workPackages.purpose: Test detector transport once on untouched target data.
workPackages.method: Apply the winning frozen operator to a WCS-selected disjoint NGC 3447 tile with a new coordinate hash.
workPackages.input: Qualified operator, disjoint tile, immutable RC71 and RC72 failures.
workPackages.output: One NRCB1 control and NRCB2 candidate decision receipt.
workPackages.pass: Support and control pass before NRCB2 effect gates, with no spatial or tail excess.
workPackages.fail: Retire the new tile and keep every downstream gate closed.
workPackages.next: Only a passing result can authorize a separately preregistered NRCB3 baseline.

uncertaintyBudget: Measurement: subpixel centering, undersampling, DQ masks, annular background, and neighbor wings dominate the rejected core integrator.
Calibration: one NRCB1 offset cannot represent detector-position PSF fraction or time-dependent focus.
Sampling: only 26-27 stars per detector-filter retained at least three valid exposures, and some cells fell below six.
Selection: catalogue support radii were explored before the CAL outcome; the experiment is transparent but not a pristine catalogue holdout.
Extrapolation: one host and two detector tiles do not establish transport to NRCB3-4, Cepheids, or H0.

connections.commonStructure: Support must precede target loss, and adjudicator qualification must precede target interpretation under an immutable adaptation graph.
connections.minimumTest: Qualify the same operator on an external isolated-star control, then transfer it once to a disjoint target tile.

claimBoundary: RC72 rejects a large-aperture support route and a small-core adjudicator for the current two-detector tiles. It does not prove NRCB2 photometry inaccurate, does not calculate a correction, does not validate a replacement PSF model, and does not estimate a Cepheid distance or Hubble constant.
exactNextStart: Do not reuse the RC72 holdout. Identify a public isolated NIRCam calibration-star dataset and preregister detector-position and subpixel-phase strata, WCS centering checks, STPSF or scene-model parameters, leave-one-exposure-out residuals, the same 0.03-mag tail and 0.02-mag spatial bounds, and an independent implementation. Only after that external control passes may a fresh disjoint NGC 3447 tile be selected.
